title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): X is a topological surface (e.g. a Riemann surface) near a point x, and U is X with finitely many points removed, x among them. D_x^* is the 'residual germ' of X at x, i.e. the germ of a punctured disc. Its category of coverings Rev(D_x^*) is Galois, cyclic with group T_x ≅ π_1(D_x^*) (≅ Z topologically). D_x^{*~} is a universal covering of this germ. The restriction functor Rev(U) → Rev(D_x^*) → Rev(D_x^{*~}) ≅ (Ens) is a fibre functor on U. It defines a fundamental group π_1(U, D_x^{*~}) and a universal covering Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}). The action of T_x on D_x^{*~} gives a homomorphism (60): T_x → π_1(U, D_x^{*~}).

If a fundamental group π = π_1(U, Ũ) has already been fixed via a universal covering Ũ, one compares the two by choosing a 'class of paths' (62). This is an isomorphism of coverings Ũ ≅ Revuniv(U, D_x^{*~}), well defined up to an element of π (equivalently of π_1(U, D_x^{*~})).

This page: the choice (62) induces an isomorphism (63) π_1(U, Ũ) ≅ π_1(U, D_x^{*~}). Changing (62) by an element of π changes (63) by an inner automorphism. Composing (63) with (60) gives a homomorphism (64) T_x → π. This depends on (62), but its class modulo inner automorphisms of π, an 'exterior' (outer) homomorphism, is well determined. It equals the outer homomorphism (65) π_1(D_x^*) → π_1(U) induced by the inclusion D_x^* ⊂ U, with π_1(D_x^*) ≅ T_x. In other words, this is the canonical construction of the inertia (local monodromy) subgroup at a puncture, defined up to conjugacy.

Section C then begins: a convenient way to fix a universal covering D_x^{*~} of D_x^* is to choose a germ of arc in X issuing from x. On the next page this is a morphism of germs [I] → D_x^*, giving a fibre functor Rev(D_x^*) → Rev([I]) ≅ (Ens). This is a topological version of a 'tangential' base point at a puncture, used to rigidify the inertia homomorphism.
errors: No mathematical errors. The bookkeeping is correct: the indeterminacy of the path class is a torsor under π, and it induces inner automorphisms on the identification of fundamental groups, so (64) is well defined as an outer homomorphism. Minor point: (60) and (62) are referenced but defined on earlier pages; the statement that (64) 'n'est autre que' (65) is asserted, not proved, though it is a routine check.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at a fibre functor given by a universal covering of a punctured-disc germ (a 'germ base point' at a puncture), and comparison with an ordinary base point via a class of paths.
ideas.modern_name: fundamental group with respect to a fibre functor / tangential base point (topological version)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (fibre functors, SGA1); tangential base points: Deligne 1989, also Ihara, Anderson
ideas.where_published: Fibre-functor formalism in SGA1; germ-of-disc base points appear in the circulated La Longue Marche (1981). Unsure whether this particular continuation is published.

ideas.what: The inclusion of the punctured disc germ defines an outer homomorphism T_x = π_1(D_x^*) → π_1(U), well defined up to conjugation; it is lifted to an actual homomorphism by choosing a path class.
ideas.modern_name: inertia subgroup / local monodromy, defined up to conjugacy
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Riemann, Hurwitz); algebraic version Grothendieck–Murre, SGA1
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame fundamental group, inertia); Esquisse d'un programme (discrete/profinite surface groups with inertia)

ideas.what: Using a germ of arc issuing from x as a base point for the punctured-disc germ, to rigidify the choice of universal covering of D_x^*.
ideas.modern_name: tangential base point / base point 'at a puncture' given by a direction or ray
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), Ihara; topologically folklore
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche (1981) or Esquisse (1984) in the guise of germ base points; not sure

missed.claim: Grothendieck (probably early 1980s) systematically developed base points at a puncture via germs of punctured discs and germs of arcs, as fibre functors on residual germs. This anticipates or parallels Deligne's 1989 tangential base points, but the content on this page is standard and the priority question belongs to the whole Longue Marche manuscript, not to this page.
missed.quote: Je vais décrire une façon commode de fixer un rev. universel D_x^{*~} de D_x^*, par un germe d'arc de courbe dans X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest for crediting the 'tangential base point' idea within anabelian geometry; no new mathematics here.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping: the inertia homomorphism is well defined up to conjugation, rigidified by a path class. The germ-of-arc base point is a mild historical anticipation of tangential base points, already associated with La Longue Marche.
transcription_corrections: In (63) the left-hand symbol looks like π with a subscript resembling 'g' (or π itself), not clearly π_x; the intended meaning is π = π_1(U, Ũ).
Under π_1(U) in (65) the symbol is an inclusion/equality sign rotated (∪ or ‖) above π, consistent with π_1(U) = π.
The marginal note under 'C) Relation avec germes d'arcs' has a crossed-out word (possibly 'origines'), then a parenthetical in quotes that is hard to read; 'groupoïde à la Godement' is uncertain.
First line: 'l'indétermination est mod un élément de π' — the crossed-out word before 'élément' appears to be a false start.
